## Root Cause Analysis

There are **two bugs** working together to produce the 403 Forbidden — one in `SecurityConfig.java` and one in `PortfolioController.java`. Neither file contains the new public endpoint at all, which is why the service tests pass (they test the service layer in isolation) while the HTTP endpoint fails.

---

### Bug 1 — `src/main/java/com/connectfolio/config/SecurityConfig.java`

**Function:** `securityFilterChain(HttpSecurity http)` — the `authorizeHttpRequests` block (lines 126–134).

**The problem:**

```java
// line 133 — this rule fires for EVERY /api/** path, including the new public one
.requestMatchers("/api/**").authenticated()
.anyRequest().permitAll()
```

The catch-all rule `.requestMatchers("/api/**").authenticated()` requires authentication for **every** path under `/api/`, including the new `GET /api/portfolios/public/{username}` endpoint. Because Spring Security evaluates rules in declaration order and stops at the first match, the public endpoint is caught by this broad rule before any more-specific `permitAll()` rule could apply — and since no such rule exists at all, unauthenticated requests are rejected with 403.

**The fix:**

Add a `permitAll()` rule for the public portfolio path **before** the broad `/api/**` authenticated rule:

```java
http.authorizeHttpRequests(auth -> auth
        .requestMatchers(STATIC_RESOURCES).permitAll()
        .requestMatchers(HttpMethod.POST, "/api/v1/users").permitAll()          // Registration
        .requestMatchers(HttpMethod.GET,  "/api/v1/portfolios/public/**").permitAll() // ← ADD THIS
        .requestMatchers("/login",
                "/oauth2/**",
                "/support/**").permitAll()
        .requestMatchers("/admin/**").hasRole("ADMIN")
        .requestMatchers("/api/**").authenticated()
        .anyRequest().permitAll());
```

The new line must appear **before** `.requestMatchers("/api/**").authenticated()` so that Spring Security's first-match evaluation reaches the `permitAll()` rule for the public path before hitting the authenticated catch-all.

---

### Bug 2 — `src/main/java/com/connectfolio/adapter/web/PortfolioController.java`

**The problem:**

The controller (`@RequestMapping("/api/v1/portfolios")`) has no handler method at all for `GET /api/portfolios/public/{username}`. The endpoint simply does not exist in the controller, so even after fixing the security config, the request would receive a 404. The endpoint needs to be implemented.

**The fix:**

Add a new handler method that maps `GET /public/{username}`, annotated with `@PreAuthorize("permitAll()")` (or no `@PreAuthorize` at all, since the security filter chain already permits it) so that method-level security — enabled by `@EnableMethodSecurity` on `SecurityConfig` — does not re-block the request:

```java
/**
 * Returns a read-only public view of a portfolio identified by the owner's username.
 * This endpoint is intentionally unauthenticated.
 */
@GetMapping("/public/{username}")
@PreAuthorize("permitAll()")          // explicit: method security must not block this
public ResponseEntity<PortfolioResponse> getPublicPortfolio(
        @PathVariable("username") String username) {

    Portfolio portfolio = getUseCase.getByUsername(username);   // delegate to existing use-case
    return ResponseEntity.ok()
                         .cacheControl(CacheControl.maxAge(Duration.ofMinutes(10)))
                         .body(mapper.toResponse(portfolio));
}
```

> **Why `@PreAuthorize("permitAll()")` is necessary:** `SecurityConfig` is annotated with `@EnableMethodSecurity`, which activates method-level security checks. Any method that lacks a `@PreAuthorize` annotation is still subject to the global filter-chain rules, but if other beans or AOP advice add a default-deny posture, being explicit prevents a future regression. More importantly, if any other method in the class carries a `@PreAuthorize` that could be inherited or if a global method security default-deny is ever added, this annotation makes the intent unambiguous.

---

### Summary of changes

| File | Location | Change |
|---|---|---|
| `src/main/java/com/connectfolio/config/SecurityConfig.java` | `securityFilterChain()` → `authorizeHttpRequests` block | Add `.requestMatchers(HttpMethod.GET, "/api/v1/portfolios/public/**").permitAll()` **before** the `/api/**` authenticated rule |
| `src/main/java/com/connectfolio/adapter/web/PortfolioController.java` | New handler method | Add `@GetMapping("/public/{username}")` with `@PreAuthorize("permitAll()")` that delegates to the existing `getUseCase` |

The security config fix is the **primary** fix — it is what causes the 403. The controller fix is the **completeness** fix — without it the endpoint returns 404 after the security gate is opened.
